cards.explanation: The answer is whoever believes in Him, friends. Jesus says, “Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’…” The water doesn't come from a spot on a map or a checklist. It flows from the person who believes in Him, and it flows from the inside.

The answer is Spirit, friends. The Gospel of John tells us straight out, “He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive.” So the living water is about the Spirit. And John doesn't leave us guessing, which I appreciate, because I've followed recipes with less help than that.

The answer is the Christ, friends. Some say, “This is truly the Prophet.” and others declare, “This is the Christ.” (John 7:40-41). Same speech, different conclusions. One invitation and the crowd is already splitting into batches.

The answer is Galilee, friends. Some in the crowd ask, “How can the Christ come from Galilee?” (John 7:41). They're saying Galilee doesn't fit what they expect. And they've got Scripture on their minds when they ask it, which I respect.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.” (John 7:43). Some said Prophet, some said Christ, and some had questions. Same words, same moment, and the crowd split every which way.

The answer is False, friends. John says, “Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.” (John 7:44). The wanting was there, but nobody followed through. That's some folks wanting to grab the dough and never getting a hand on it.

The answer is “Never has anyone spoken like this man,” friends. The officers answer, “Never has anyone spoken like this man!” (John 7:46). Remember, they were sent to bring Jesus in (John 7:32). And they came back with that answer instead of Him.
The answer is False, friends. The Pharisees don't agree with the officers. They reply, “Have you also been deceived?” (John 7:47). Instead of agreeing, they ask the officers if they've been fooled.
The answer is curse, friends. The Pharisees say, “But this crowd that does not know the law—they are under a curse.” (John 7:49). Curse is the word the text gives them.

The answer is whether the law convicts a man before hearing him, friends. Nicodemus asks, “Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?” (John 7:51). He's asking about their own law, in front of the group he belongs to. I think that took guts.
The answer is True, friends. The others answer Nicodemus, “Aren’t you also from Galilee?” (John 7:52). They don't answer his question about the law at all. They turn it right back around on him.
